analysis.title: Golar LNG (GLNG): First Take: 3Q26 Above Consensus, Starting Boat Five Development, but Quieter on Boat Four Commercialization
key_insights: GLNG (Buy) reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $56m, 12% below GSe of $64m and 11% above FactSet consensus of $50m. Lower commodity-linked revenues drove the miss versus GS, while overall operations appeared strong.

No commercial announcement on the fourth FLNG vessel came with the release. GLNG ordered the fourth boat at 2Q26 results and said commercialization could follow a pace similar to Esperanza, which could mean final terms in 1H27, though recent customer discussions appeared to be moving faster.

Management reserved long-lead equipment for a fifth FLNG vessel to allow delivery in three years, citing strong customer interest. GS still sees any fifth-vessel order following commercialization of the fourth.

FLNG segment adj. EBITDA was $65m versus GSe of $73m. The miss came from lower commodity-linked revenues on the derivative realization tied to Hilli. GS had modeled one full month of Hilli, but the charter concluded on July 27.

Gimi continued to overproduce, but the YTD invoiced day rate premium over the contracted day rate moderated to 12% from 17% at 2Q26 on warm ambient temperatures and scheduled maintenance. Management expects the premium to rebuild gradually as temperatures cool into late 4Q26.
Corporate adj. EBITDA of -$9m was in line with GSe, as vessel operating revenues, expenses and G&A were in line.
FLNG Esperanza conversion is on track for 4Q27 delivery and on budget, with onshore work also on track. GLNG has spent $1.6b of $2.2b total project cost, up from $1.4b at 2Q26.

Hilli refurbishment is underway at the Seatrium shipyard and the asset remains on track for mid-2027 in-service in Argentina. Management reiterated guided run-rate EBITDA of $400m (ex-commodity) on Hilli and Esperanza in Argentina, with potential upside over time.

Management noted financing progress that effectively secures significant liquidity for boat four, and progress on contracting at SESA, which helps start locking in the price-related upside in the Argentina contracts coming on next year.

At GS's early October management meeting, management cited robust customer demand for the fourth vessel, advancing negotiations with multiple prospective customers, a narrowing bid-ask on contract terms, and confidence in announcing a customer commitment in the near term.

There was no update on the strategic review announced in March, which is focused on accelerating the FLNG growth pipeline and maximizing shareholder value, with alternatives including a sale of the company. GS looks for the next update after the board meeting in mid-November but expects limited call commentary.

GS price target and estimates are unchanged ahead of the earnings call. Questions expected on boat four terms, timing, counterparty and returns, future FLNG demand by geography, fifth vessel FID timing, LNG offtake demand, rates versus Argentina contracts, the strategic review, and crystallizing commodity option value in Argentina.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $67 12-month target unchanged after the 3Q26 print. Stock closed at $41.94 on 17 Nov 2026, implying 59.8% upside.

earnings_insights: GLNG 3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $56m versus GSe $64m and FactSet consensus $50m. It was $127m in 2Q26 and $83m in 3Q25.

FLNG segment adj. EBITDA reported $65m versus GSe $73m. FLNG revenues reported $94m versus GSe $91m, and commodity-linked revenues reported $0 versus GSe $10m. FLNG operating expenses were $32m versus GSe $23m.
Corporate adj. EBITDA reported -$9m versus GSe of -$9m. The dividend was $0.25 per share, in line with GSe.
GS forecasts (estimates): 12/26E EPS $1.59, EBITDA $339.9m. 12/27E EPS $1.00, EBITDA $288.6m. 12/28E EPS $3.29, EBITDA $636.0m. 9/26E quarterly EPS is estimated at $0.33.
Esperanza project spend to date is $1.6b of $2.2b total, and guided run-rate EBITDA is $400m ex-commodity for Hilli plus Esperanza once operating in Argentina.
risk_factors: Higher than expected conversion costs and longer than expected conversion timelines
Complex or atypical financing arrangements weighing on perceived transparency
